newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures rise on yen's dip.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures rise on yen's dip.

text.p: Yen-based gold futures extended their gains to end at the day's highs on Wednesday, buoyed by the yen's further fall against the dollar following the results of the U.S. election, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from nine to 12 yen per gram higher, with the key October contract ending 10 yen up at 1,379 yen.
The bullion market reacted little to the election results as the market had discounted a win by President Clinton and projections the Republicans would take both houses of Congress.
Spot gold was quoted at $378.85/379.15 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $378.80/379.30 in New York on Tuesday.
Activity in both gold futures and the bullion market was lacklustre.

Traders said Japanese traders were tending to take moderately bullish views on gold futures, based on a perception that the yen's weaker tendency will continue, while they agreed upper resistance at $380.00 would be hard to break through for the near term.

"As long as U.S. stocks stay firm, more fund money is unlikely to pour into the gold market. Gold is unlikely to stray away from a range of between $377.50 and $380.00 for the near-term," one trader said.
Platinum futures settled firmer on the heels of gold, while silver and palladium futures were mostly up in sluggish trade.
Platinum futures ranged from two to six yen per gram up. Benchmark October was six yen higher at 1,390 yen.
Weaker spot platinum prices limited gains in platinum futures, traders said.
Benchmark October silver contract finished 1.2 yen per 10 grams up at 180.7 yen. Benchmark October palladium ended two yen firmer at 428 yen.
